hints: Focus on what alkaline iodine is really testing for, the iodoform reaction needs a specific little group in the molecule.
Look for alcohols containing the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ unit, then check what is attached to that carbon besides the methyl group.
Remember the rest of the molecule becomes the carboxylate, so to get a 2-carbon ethanoate you need a 1-carbon group left behind.
walkthrough:
**Recall the iodoform condition**

Great start, let's remember the rule together. Alkaline $\text{I}_2$ gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ only with a methyl carbonyl $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group or a methyl alcohol $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group that can be oxidised to it.

General reaction:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-\text{R} + \text{I}_2 + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3 + \text{RCOO}^-$$

**See what the R group becomes**

This is the clever part. The $\text{CH}_3$ part is lost as triiodomethane, and whatever R group was attached is left as the carboxylate ion $\text{RCOO}^-$.

So to make ethanoate $\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-$, we need $\text{R} = \text{CH}_3$.

**Check each alcohol**

Now let's test our alcohols. Ethanol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, so $\text{R} = \text{H}$ and it would give methanoate $\text{HCOO}^-$. Butan-2-ol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, so $\text{R} = \text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and it would give propanoate.

Propan-2-ol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$, so $\text{R} = \text{CH}_3$, perfect for ethanoate $\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-$.

options.A: Ethanol $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ does give a positive iodoform test, but its R group is H. It produces methanoate ions $\text{HCOO}^-$, not ethanoate ions, so this is a very tempting trap.
options.B: Methylpropan-2-ol, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{COH}$, is a tertiary alcohol with no hydrogen on the carbon bearing the OH. It cannot be oxidised and has no $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group, so no reaction occurs.
options.C: Propan-2-ol $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$ contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group with $\text{R} = \text{CH}_3$. Oxidation and cleavage with alkaline $\text{I}_2$ gives $\text{CHI}_3$ plus ethanoate $\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-$, exactly as required.
options.D: Butan-2-ol $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ does react to give $\text{CHI}_3$, but its R group is ethyl $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-$. It therefore produces propanoate ions $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-$, not ethanoate.
